description.short_caption: Axial CT scan of the abdomen showing multiple fluid and gas-filled loops of bowel.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the abdomen demonstrates multiple dilated loops of bowel with fluid and gas, suggestive of bowel obstruction or ileus. There is evidence of a thickened bowel wall in some segments, and the presence of free air or fluid is not clearly visible. The surrounding abdominal structures appear unremarkable. No contrast enhancement is evident, suggesting this is a non-contrast study.
visible_findings: fluid and gas within bowel loops
thickened bowel wall in some segments

description.short_caption: Axial CT scan of the pelvis showing a large central pelvic mass.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the pelvis demonstrates a large, well-defined, centrally located pelvic mass. The mass appears to be hypodense relative to surrounding soft tissues. Adjacent structures, including the pelvic bones and soft tissues, are visible. There is no clear evidence of contrast enhancement in this image, suggesting it may be a non-contrast study.
visible_findings: adjacent pelvic bones and soft tissues visible

Case_04024/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Figure 3. Mycobacterium tuberculosis from renal aspirate, acid-fast stain.

description.short_caption: Acid-fast bacilli in renal aspirate, consistent with Mycobacterium species.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a cluster of red, rod-shaped bacilli against a pale background, stained using an acid-fast technique. The red coloration indicates the presence of acid-fast organisms, consistent with Mycobacterium species. The bacilli are arranged in a slightly clumped formation, characteristic of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The background appears lightly stained, with no other prominent structures visible.
